reason: Conversation 2 told the homeowner to isolate at the cooker switch (not just the controls), to remove the glass lamp cover first, and to confirm the rating from the old bulb before buying, then confirmed the E14 25W 300C match and gave a sensible fallback (lamp holder/wiring -> engineer) if the new bulb does not work. Conversation 1 reached the right bulb type but omitted the lamp cover step and the isolator, asserted the spec without asking the homeowner to verify against the old bulb, and gave no guidance on what to do if the replacement fails. Both correctly warned against ordinary household bulbs, but 2 was safer, more complete, and better aligned with the expected first step and escalation path.
